title: The Barriers Facing Net Zero Laws for Natural Gas Utilities
content: North America and Europe have a wide variety of laws specifying a future year (most often ending in zero) by which the state, province or country aims to achieve a net-zero decarbonization target. Having such targets, various state/provincial or national agencies or regulators have taken various actions to limit the expansion of natural gas utilities, change the means of accounting for pipeline capital projects, initiate decarbonization pilot projects, and/or otherwise plan for a decarbonization trajectory regarding natural gas distribution companies that would serve to help meet those net-zero legislative goals (Table 1). The question regarding all these aspirational net zero laws: will they work in the end? Put another way, are those laws ultimately only aspirational, or might they constitute binding limits against which the regulators of natural gas distributors, or other agencies in charge, can plan the wind-down of natural gas public service firms?
